To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) our model achieves state-of-the-art results on standard entity linking benchmarks, 2) the model can be estimated using unlabeled texts, and 3) modeling unlabeled documents improves the performance over modeling Wikipedia alone.

(a) we present a method for entity linking that does not rely on labeled documents, (b) we show that this method is effective in the challenging setting of entity linking, and (c) we show that the method is effective even when trained on unlabeled documents.

(i) entity linking can be performed on unlabeled documents, (ii) unlabeled documents can improve the quality of the resulting system, (iii) our approach rivals the state of the art on standard test sets, (iv) it is the first to achieve comparable performance on a test set from the training data, and (v) our system outperforms a Wikipedia-only system.
